statement: At the pinned instrument research_map/astra_lifecycle.py#957c61e3eb0e and the byte-frozen reviews/ corpus 42e9cee5a43ce36f (225 files), the controller coverage scan counts a full accept only when a target string normalises to a node id AND an explicit pin string matches the measured sha256 prefix; it therefore reports F1 4 / F2a 2 / F2b 3 full accepts while two further live full accepts are invisible to it (F1 ['F1-review-worker-089.json'], F2a ['F2a-review-18-rev13.json']), each binding the live schema sha256 through a path#hash target or an artifact_sha256 pin. The live instrument (548329414083) carries byte-identical coverage functions, so the same rule and the same blind spots hold at live bytes. Measured blind-spot census over the frozen corpus: 22 path#hash + 1 node#hash + 2 node@hash targets, 5 multi-targets, 9 class_id-only targets, 7 dict-valued reviewed_sha256, and 87 verdict files whose counts_as_full_schema_verdict is null and therefore treated as full. The proposed UNAPPLIED patch (proposed_patch.diff) recovers the two accepts and reports F1 5 / F2a 3 / F2b 3 with no lost accept and no false positive; 11/11 controls pass and two runs over the identical frozen corpus are byte-identical.
